original_value: Fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs) have the potential to be used as flexible power plants in future energy systems. To integrate FCEVs through vehicle‐to‐grid (V2G), agreements are needed between the FCEV owners and the actor that coordinates V2G on behalf of them, usually considered the aggregator. In this paper, we argue that, depending on the purpose of providing V2G and the goal of the system or the aggregator, different types of contracts are needed, not currently considered in the literature. We propose price‐based, volume‐based, and control‐based contracts. Using agent‐based modeling and simulation we show how price‐based contracts can be applied for selling V2G in the wholesale electricity market and how volume‐based contracts can be used for balancing the local energy supply and demand in a microgrid. The models can provide a base to explore strategies in the market and to improve performance in a system highly dependent on V2G.

result.paraphrase: Fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs) could serve as flexible power plants in future energy systems. To integrate them via vehicle-to-grid (V2G), agreements are required between FCEV owners and the party coordinating V2G on their behalf, typically the aggregator. In this paper, we contend that the contract type should vary with the purpose of V2G provision and the objectives of the system or aggregator, and that the literature has not yet considered these different needs. We introduce price-based, volume-based, and control-based contracts. Through agent-based modeling and simulation, we demonstrate how price-based contracts can support V2G sales in the wholesale electricity market and how volume-based contracts can help balance local supply and demand in a microgrid. These models offer a foundation for exploring market strategies and improving performance in a system that depends heavily on V2G.
